title: mcp: a host can observe and refuse every MCP tool call through one neutral interceptor (cloud#3820 O2)
body:
repo:cloud#3 · os-zhuang · session_01QUs3BvRcDHXqRU4TSVE4u6

Filing gate: ③ maintainer-dispatched task, child of objectstack-ai/cloud#3820 (EE AI employee console, p1). Maintainer, 2026-11-08 16:27 UTC, in the cloud#3820 PM thread: 「objectstack 可以先开工吗？」. The PM thread read this as "start the open-source tasks that depend on nothing", and O1, O2 and O5 are those tasks.

Parent: objectstack-ai/cloud#3820, card 0 (external AI under governance). Consumers in cloud after a pin: C1 (audit row per MCP call), C2 (AI seat check on the MCP door), C4 (kill switch).

## 维护者速读

外部 AI 通过 MCP 调用数据工具时，直接走数据协议，任何宿主都看不见、也拦不住这次调用。所以企业版的 AI 审计表里没有外部 AI 的记录。这张卡在 MCP 门上加一个中立的拦截口：默认什么都不装，行为不变；企业版装上后可以记审计、按席位或停用状态拒绝。开源侧不含任何许可逻辑和审计表。

## Problem (read in code at objectstack 3c380253, not run)

- HTTP `/mcp` tools reach data through `callData` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` around line 930 for create, update and remove; query, get and aggregate the same way), never through the AI `ToolRegistry`.
- The `ToolRegistry` has a neutral `setInterceptor` seam. Cloud's EE governance uses it to audit and veto in-product AI tool calls. MCP has no equivalent, so on a licensed EE an external AI's calls never reach `sys_ai_audit_log`.
- Per-request HTTP servers register tools through `wireBridgeTools` (object, action and file tools) and `registerAuthoringTools`. The long-lived stdio server registers through `bridgeDataTools` and `bridgeTools` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` around lines 1254, 1413 and 1454).
- `bridgeTools` calls `toolRegistry.execute(call)` with no context. Under EE governance every such call is denied as `denied_no_actor`, so the stdio bridge of AI tools is unusable there.

## Do

1. Add a host-installable interceptor on the `mcp` service, for example `setToolInterceptor(fn)`. When none is set, behaviour is byte-identical to today.
2. Route every tool call on every path through it: the HTTP object, action and file tools, the authoring family, and the stdio `bridgeDataTools` and `bridgeTools`.
3. Pass a server-constructed context: door (`mcp`), transport (http or stdio), tool name, arguments, and the principal (`userId`, `principalKind`, `onBehalfOf`, `performedBy.clientId`, `organizationId`, `environmentId`). Nothing from client headers. O4 will add the service-account key to `performedBy`.
4. Contract: the interceptor calls `next()` (allow; it sees the result and may replace it) or returns a refusal without calling `next()` (deny), answered with the existing coded-refusal envelope. Leave room for a later "hold" outcome (cloud#3820 O6, route to `plugin-approvals`) but do not build it.
5. Give `bridgeTools` the stdio principal as its execution context, so a governed host sees an actor.
6. No licence logic and no audit table in open code, the same rule as `ToolRegistry.setInterceptor`.

## Tests

- Unset: the existing MCP suites stay green unchanged.
- Allow, deny and replace on each registration path (HTTP data, actions, files, authoring; stdio data and bridged tools).
- The principal fields cannot be changed by any request header.

## Done when

Merged, with the single-node, no-interceptor behaviour unchanged. Cloud consumes it after a pin.

## Reader

Filed and dispatched by a cloud seat; reviewed and landed by that seat. The cloud#3820 PM thread answers premise questions.

Dedup: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue interceptor mcp` and `mcp tool call audit` returned no card about an MCP tool-call seam (#27908, closed, recorded the action door only).

## Duplicates

Searched objectstack open issues for "service account" AI, MCP interceptor, OAuth client disable token, API key suspend (2026-11-08): no open card covers this.
